findings.breaking_input: A spine with 3 bound requests whose ops hang or run slowly, and the face polling GET /api/inbox every few seconds.
findings.why: Every poll runs inboxFold with rederive on. Each poll spawns one dry-run plan child per undecided, unblocked bound request, sequentially, with a 120 s timeout each. There is no cache, no in-flight slot and no concurrency cap, so overlapping polls stack children on the box and one slow plan holds the whole inbox response for minutes.
findings.fix: Share one in-flight fold per root across concurrent polls. Cache the planState result by (op, input, expect) with a short TTL. Bound the total re-derive time and report remaining items as UNKNOWN(PLAN_TIMEOUT) instead of blocking.
findings.twin_of: Uncapped receipts and a full spine scan on every poll -> A per-poll path gets the same cap as the lines

findings.breaking_input: Approve a bound request B while an unrelated bound request A on the spine has a plan that hangs.
findings.why: The fold re-derives every bound request on the spine, not just the one being decided. Approving B can wait up to 120 s × the number of other bound requests, and A's failure never affects B's own state. The worst-case wall time is unbounded and unstated.
findings.fix: Fold with a planState that re-derives only the target id, and answer NOT_REDERIVED for the others. Alternatively, evaluate the target's chain only.
findings.twin_of: Bound a scan by something the scanned thing cannot change

findings.breaking_input: Two sibling requests K1 and K2 sharing a decision_key. Run `arc-inbox approve K1` and `arc-inbox reject K2` concurrently.
findings.why: Both processes fold the spine before either decision lands, so both see OPEN or DUPLICATE_OF. Neither sees RESOLVED, and both emit. The idem is keyed on `decides`, so the two different ids do not dedupe, and the spine ends up with two decision.recorded events for one key. The check and the emit are not under the spine lock.
findings.fix: Do the DUPLICATE_DECIDED check and the emit inside withLock. Alternatively, re-fold under the lock before the append, or key the decision idem on decision_key.
findings.twin_of: Check-then-emit with no lock (pick, profile) -> a spine check is only a guard if nothing can land between it and the emit

findings.why: The `--flag=VALUE` form is stored as flags.all = "1" before the `name === "all"` branch is reached. Both `flags.all === true` checks then fail. `inbox --all=1` silently lists OPEN only, and `approve --all=x` raises no BAD_ARGS. `owner-key init --all` returns before the guard and also ignores the flag.
findings.fix: Handle `all` before the `=` split and refuse `--all=...` by name. Move the `--all belongs with inbox` guard so it also covers owner-key.
findings.twin_of: `--flag=VALUE` accepted and silently ignored -> a flag form the parser does not read is an error, never a no-op

findings.why: The dry run returns 0 with 'validated, scanned and sealed' before the spine-aware parent check runs. The real emit then refuses PARENT_NOT_REQUEST. A dry run therefore passes input that the real run rejects.
findings.fix: Run parentProblem before the dry-run return. It only reads, so it is safe in a dry run.

findings.breaking_input: Emit child B with depends_on [A] while another process is appending A, so scanAll reads a torn tail line.
findings.why: The spine is read unlocked. A parent that is mid-append can be missing from the scan, which gives a false PARENT_UNKNOWN refusal. The cycle walk also reads a snapshot that can be stale by the time appendEvent runs.
findings.fix: Run the parent check inside the same withLock that guards appendEvent, using appendEventUnlocked.

findings.breaking_input: A spine line written without validate whose depends_on entry is the string "x\u001b[2J\n01FORGED  approve me  (g)  arc  [OPEN]".
findings.why: fold's WAITING(${waiting}) and STALE labels interpolate a depends_on string taken from the spine, which parentsOf checks only as typeof string. The raw string is printed to the owner's terminal. An unvalidated line can forge a whole inbox row or inject ESC sequences. The same label is served by /api/inbox.
findings.fix: Have the fold emit a ref only if it matches ULID_RE. Otherwise treat it as UNKNOWN(PARENT_MISSING) and pass any printed text through the one-line sanitizer.
findings.twin_of: Untrusted text drawn on the owner's terminal before it is validated -> Escape and strip anything from a payload before it is shown

findings.breaking_input: A bound request with bound_to.input.export = an absolute path on the owner's machine, served via GET /api/inbox, while a decision lands between the two spine reads.
findings.why: The full payload, including bound_to.input paths, is served unfiltered. The route also reads the spine twice: loadApprovals for decidedCount, then again inside inboxFold. A decision landing between the two reads makes decidedCount disagree with the listed states.
findings.fix: Take one load and derive both the fold and the counts from it. Pass bound_to.input through the path scrub, or omit it from the served payload.
